newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to further develop Statfjord oilfield.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to further develop Statfjord oilfield.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had presented a recommendation to develop the northern flank of the Statfjord oilfield with two subsea templates.
They would be tied back to the C platform about eight kilometres away, Statoil's newsletter Status Weekly said.
"This part of the North Sea field is thought to contain some 85 million barrels of recoverable oil and 2.5 billion standard cubic metres of gas," the newsletter said.
One template will support four production wells, while the other is to contain two water injectors.

"The alternative approach of tapping these reserves with extended-reach wells from Statfjord C would substantially defer the platform's own output," Oeyvind Haugane, manager for Statfjord development projects, said.

"Viewing the Statfjord area as a whole, the recommended subsea solution offers good flexibility with an eye to other developments which might be pursued later," he said. "Its economics are also very good."

Northern-flank production could last almost to the end of Statfjord C's producing life, around 2020. The proposed development solution will be considered by the licensees in August, Status Weekly added.
